_comment: Path -> owning skills. The ONLY place this mapping lives; a new concern is a new row here, not
another paragraph in an AGENTS.md nobody reads. skill_router.py enforces it on Write/Edit, and
the review skill reads the same table so a review cannot miss what an author was required to load.
EVERY matching row fires, not the first. So the table is layered on purpose: the two area floors
and the four layer rows at the top always apply, and a specific row below ADDS to them rather than
replacing them. That is what makes coverage total - routing on filename suffix only ever covers the
names someone thought to enumerate, and a `Mappers.cs` rule silently missed every `XMapper.cs`.
Prefer a row keyed on the layer or area a file lives in; reach for a name-shaped row only to refine.
path    : regex matched against the repo-relative POSIX path.

skills  : must be invoked before writing this file. `plugin:skill` where a generic standard and this system's roster share a name - both load, and the plugin says which is which. A name with one home stays bare. The router quotes each skill's own description rather than restating rules, so there is exactly one copy.
note    : optional; shown with the row when it fires. For why a row exists, not for restating a rule.
deny    : regex matched against the content being written. A hit is a hard block, not a nudge -

routes.note: Area floor. Every C# file gets the style and naming standard, so a shape nobody wrote a route for is still gated. Specific routes below add to this, they do not replace it.
Area floor, same reason as the .NET one above.
Layer route. Keyed on the layer the project name declares rather than on a filename suffix, because a suffix rule only covers the names someone thought to enumerate.

deny.reason: This is a *.UnitTests project and this code boots a host, container or database. That makes it an integration test. Put it in this service's *.IntegrationTests project, which owns the fixture that boots the real Program. The build enforces this too (api/TestConventions.targets).

routes.note: Creating a test project is the classification moment: decide unit vs integration BEFORE the name exists, because the name is what declares the tier and the build fails a name that states none.
A context IS a tenancy stance - which base it derives from decides what every query through it can see. Only B2B has tenanted stances; the per-module roster is api/Concertable.B2B/CODE_PATTERNS.md.
Mapping a table another module owns needs ExcludeFromMigrations here, or two migrations claim the same table.
A state change announces itself by raising on the entity; the pre-commit handler is what turns that into a published integration event, so the outbox row commits with the write.

The rule whose violation is silent and expensive: a seeder may only write what production code writes directly. If the only production write is a handler reacting to an event, drive the event. The forbidden-table roster is the seeding skill.
A data service WaitFor-ing another data service is the bug to never introduce. The live topology is api/ARCHITECTURE.md.

Build and package config is per service folder by design - there is deliberately no repo-root version or build config, because a carve takes only the service folder and would leave anything above it behind.

The lifecycle rules a plan or ledger must satisfy - what each artifact is, when it is deleted, the two dependency graphs, cross-plan blockers. This repo's layout, hooks and commands are plans/AGENTS.md and plans/agents/.
This file is only the exact shape of the continuation pointer; the rule that a non-terminal plan must emit one belongs to the skill.
Debt is recorded in the TECH_DEBT.md of the area that owns the problem, and the whole entry is deleted once fixed - never kept as an archive.
Writing guidance is the moment one-rule-one-home is won or lost: check docs/INDEX.md for an existing owner first, and never add a second copy of a rule that already has one.
